references.text: The preceding parable of the lost sheep follows the same pattern: something valuable is lost, the owner searches diligently, and there is great joy when what was lost is found. The parable of the lost coin in [ref:Luk 15:8|Luke 15:8] is a parallel to the parable of the lost sheep in [ref:Luk 15:4-7|Luke 15:4-7], and both illustrate God's eagerness to seek out what is lost.

The continuation in [ref:Luk 15:9-10|Luke 15:9-10] describes the joy when the coin is found, and Jesus draws the spiritual parallel: there is joy among God's angels over one sinner who repents. Verse 8 is the beginning of this parable that points forward to this conclusion.

The parable of the prodigal son in [ref:Luk 15:11-32|Luke 15:11-32] is the third parable in the same chapter, following the same theme of what was lost being found again, but now expanded to deal with a father and his two sons, showing even deeper God's love and grace.

In [ref:Luk 19:10|Luke 19:10] Jesus says: "For the Son of Man has come to seek and to save what was lost." This summarizes the same motif that lies behind the parable of the lost coin – God actively seeks what is lost.

In [ref:Esek 34:11-16|Ezekiel 34:11-16] God Himself promises to seek out His sheep that are scattered and go out to find them. This Old Testament text provides the background for the image of God actively seeking what is lost, just as the woman in the parable searches carefully for her lost coin.

In [ref:Matt 18:12-14|Matthew 18:12-14] Jesus tells a similar parable about the lost sheep and emphasizes that it is not the Father's will that any of these little ones should perish. This shares the fundamental theme with the parable of the lost coin: God's diligent search for what is lost.

In [ref:Ordsp 2:4-5|Proverbs 2:4-5] one is urged to seek wisdom as if it were hidden treasures, with the same eagerness and care that the woman shows when she searches for her lost coin. The image of diligent searching is common.

In [ref:Sef 1:12|Zephaniah 1:12] the Lord describes how He will search Jerusalem with lamps, which reflects the image in [ref:Luk 15:8|Luke 15:8] where the woman lights a lamp to search for her coin. Both texts use the image of lighting a lamp to search thoroughly.
